reason: Despite a wrong opening citation, it concludes from the material that a tenant is a mere holder (tenedor) who cannot acquire by usucapión, which supports 'no'.
Clumsy reasoning about express mandate, but it derives 'tak' from the owner's written confirmation of the lease, which is the point the question turns on.
It identifies art. 7 LAR non-application for developable land and the 1-year notice from the material; the LAU slip is a side point.
It states from the material that the community can use the proceso monitorio against the registered owner.
It applies art. 25 LCCI (ordinary rate + 3 points) to the 3% rate and gets 6%.
Brief but it applies the material's life-usufruct formula of 89 minus age to get 29%.
It takes the 60 business days for tanteo from the material's art. 22 LAR rule.
It applies art. 30 CC's live-birth requirement to the stillbirth and concludes no legal personality.
It applies 10% of the budget net of machinery (art. 22 LISTA) and computes 139,500 euros correctly.
It uses the rogación principle and the art. 82 LH note that lapse cancellation needs a request from a registered right holder.
It picks the 1% Andalusian AJD rate for a habitual residence at or under 150k and computes 670 euros.
It states from the material that in a ZMRT the threshold can be lowered to 5 or more residential properties.
It identifies the SL as a legal person and applies the material's 30-year maximum.
It contrasts the informative nota simple with the authoritative certification and matches the quick-check need to the nota simple.
It applies art. 1508 CC's 4-year default when no term is agreed.
It applies the 99% Group I/II bonus (art. 39) to the stated tax and computes 793.60 euros.
It states that the registry certification is the only authoritative Registry document and is used in court.
It names art. 1451 CC as regulating the bilateral promise to sell, which the material's citations list says; the wrong tema label is a side point.
It applies the participation quota to the cost and computes 23,393.80 euros.
It attributes the 99% to the wrong provision, but it applies a 99% relief from the material to the tax and derives 840.90 euros.
It identifies the gift as inofficious and, per the material, reducible by the forced heirs; the wrong article number is a side point.
It cites art. 205 LH from the material: double public title needs at least a 1-year gap.
It classifies the shop as other use, applies the 2-month deposit, and the 7,100 euros follows from 2 times 3,550.
It applies the 30% conformity reduction and then 40% off the remainder, and computes 33,415.20 euros step by step.
The first sentence is garbled, but it correctly derives the 5% limit without a fully matching CCDG under art. 201.3 LH.
It applies 10% of the budget net of machinery under art. 22 LISTA and computes 79,600 euros.
Despite irrelevant tanteo text, it applies the art. 1.2 LAR source hierarchy to put the parties' agreement first.
After a detour into retracto, it applies art. 399 CC: a co-owner sells her share without others' consent.
It states the 3/5 majority for VUT approval from art. 17.12 LPH as given in the material.
It applies the art. 9 LAR rule that non-EU/EEA, non-resident, non-reciprocity foreigners cannot be tenants.
It applies art. 7 LAR: when land becomes developable mid-lease, the landlord can terminate on 1 year's notice.
It states the dación en pago exemption requires no other sufficient assets and concludes the condition fails, so no exemption.
It applies the material's constitutive vs. declarative distinction: a mortgage exists as a real right only once registered.
It places the ground (serious harm with no duty to bear) under art. 18 LPH, confirms standing, and applies the general 3-month deadline rather than the 1-year one for illegality.
It cites the material's rule that special VUT quotas are non-retroactive, so earlier years cannot be charged.
It applies art. 530 CC and nemine res sua servit: an easement needs different owners.
It mislabels the gift type, but it treats the breach as non-performance of a charge (art. 647 CC) and gives 4 years from breach.

It says division needs the co-owners' unanimity and cannot proceed without the others' consent, which points to 'nie', yet it ends 'tak' without stating that art. 400 CC lets any co-owner demand division absent a pact.
It applies the 10% partial-sublease increase from art. 32 LAU and computes 9,130 euros.
It applies art. 451 CC: a good-faith possessor keeps the fruits received before interruption, so no.
